checks: Every constituent is relatively open in the closed nonnegative quadrant, so arbitrary unions and their tails are measurable. The bounded intercepts give finite areas.

For a tail point in a constituent, b>s. After scaling, its normalized sum is strictly below (1−s/b)/r≤1. The common affine map is injective and its image remains in that same constituent, so the entire tail maps into U without overlap multiplicity.
The determinant gives r². A constituent with b=B has its entire domain equal to the image of its tail, up to the stated strict boundaries. Verified r=64/167 and r²<3/20 exactly.
The bound and constants match 94bf8f29da63e55b §3 (16)–(18); the one-constituent equality follows by the inverse map.

overlap.comparison: Controls loss in a strip using radial convex weights on a simplex facet, with nested homothet hypotheses. This result is a sharp area fraction for arbitrary unions of coordinate triangles and keeps overlaps by one common injection.

readability: The statement and proof are readable as written.
review_method: Independent cold proof and archived-source review, with a separate exact symbolic or rational check where applicable.
summary: The same affine contraction works on the full union tail, with the sharp factor for the stated family.
